incident-bot: 🔔 ALERT 20:12 UTC — continuous-batcher service in us-east-1 is reporting sustained latency > 5s and repeated OOMs on gpu-worker pods (auto-detected by anomaly-detector). Rolling error rate increasing on /v1/generate for model-redwood-7b-quant.

alex-ruiz: seeing the same from dashboards. P95 spiked from 200ms -> 6s. Pod restarts count jumped, some pods OOMKilled by OOM-killer. Suspect batch growth deadlock.

maya-chen: confirmed. kube events show repeated evictions: "OOMKilled" then node flaps (kubelet registering NotReady briefly). nvml reports driver errors on node gpu-12.

samir-patel: can someone grab the last 100 lines from one of the failing pods? i'm on it.

jess_l: grabbing logs now, posting snippet.```
2026-03-15T20:09:41Z continuous-batcher[pid:4123] WARN batcher: queue length 1250, max_batch_size 512
2026-03-15T20:09:41Z continuous-batcher ERROR allocation failed: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
2026-03-15T20:09:42Z kernel: docker invoked oom-killer: gfp_mask=0x24000c0
2026-03-15T20:09:43Z kubelet: Back-off restarting failed container
``` 

maya-chen: thanks. That cudaMalloc failure plus queue length >> max_batch_size is classic runaway-batch growth. Looks like the prefix caching wasn't applying and KV sizes exploded.

alex-ruiz: immediate mitigation options: 1) disable continuous batching (feature flag) to fall back to request-level batching, 2) scale down max concurrent requests per worker (env), 3) drain affected nodes and restart gpu drivers. We should pick 1+3 now.

samir-patel: agree. I'll flip the FF for continuous-batcher in prod to OFF and push a config patch. Patch command:```
# flip feature flag via infra-control
infractl feature set continuous_batching false --env=prod --region=us-east-1
``` 

ops-bot: infractl: started feature toggle job id=ff-29831. Expected propagation 30s — 2m.

jess_l: while that propagates, i'm cordoning and draining the most flappy node (gpu-12) to force pods to reschedule. Going to `kubectl cordon gpu-12` then `kubectl drain gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`.

maya-chen: be careful — draining will move traffic to other nodes that are also near capacity. We should also temporarily reduce replicaCount for continuous-batcher to limit concurrency until FF fully rolls out.

alex-ruiz: good catch. Set replicas from 16 -> 8 for the deployment in us-east-1.

samir-patel: scaling down replicas now:```
kubectl scale deploy/continuous-batcher -n prod --replicas=8 --context=us-east-1
``` 

incident-bot: ff-29831: feature toggle COMPLETE. continuous_batching=false in us-east-1 applied to 95% of routes.

jess_l: drain started on gpu-12; some pods evicted and rescheduled. Observing transient increase in 500s as connections move.

maya-chen: checking model fallback: route /v1/generate for customer-1422 was pinned to redwood-7b-quant; i'd like to route heavy customers to a lower-memory variant while we stabilize. Can we set policy to route large-token requests to redwood-3b-quant temporarily?

alex-ruiz: doing policy patch:```
policyctl set-route /v1/generate --customer=1422 --model=redwood-3b-quant --region=us-east-1
``` 

ops-bot: policy change accepted. route update id=pol-7732.

samir-patel: monitoring logs — CUDA errors dropping, pod OOMs decreasing. P95 coming down to ~1.2s after FF and scaling changes.

jess_l: node gpu-12 drained and rebooting NV driver (sudo systemctl restart nvidia-docker). will rejoin when healthy.

maya-chen: customer-impact note: support dashboard shows Customer-1422 and a handful of PLG users saw 503 spikes from 20:08–20:25 UTC. We'll draft a status update once we confirm stable.

alex-ruiz: summary of mitigations performed:
- flipped continuous batching FF off in us-east-1
- scaled continuous-batcher replicas 16->8
- cordoned + drained gpu-12 and restarted NV driver
- route policy set for heavy customer to 3b quant
- will monitor for 30m, oncall handoff at 21:00 UTC

jess_l: metric snapshot: error-rate peak 18% at 20:11, down to 0.9% at 20:35. CPU/GPU utilization normalized on rescheduled pods.

maya-chen: i'm collecting core dumps and attaching to incident ticket. For postmortem we should capture: why prefix/KV cache didn't trim large entries, why batch-growth guard didn't limit queue length, and whether a recent kernel/driver bump correlated with increased OOMs on gpu-12.

samir-patel: noted. i'll create a short runbook entry about an emergency knob: max_queue_len env + fail-open target which we briefly exercised.

oncall-next: i'm taking handoff at 21:00 UTC and will watch the routemap + alerts. Please DM if anything regresses. I'll keep paged rotation updated.

alex-ruiz: thanks. Final ops note: keep continuous batching disabled until we push a guarded rollout with stricter queue caps and KV eviction policy. Postmortem owners: maya + samir + runtime-qa.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: error-rate returned to baseline and pods stabilized. Incident duration 00:27. Severity: Sev2. Follow-up: runbook + postmortem assigned.

jess_l: i'll draft a short public note for status.redwood.com and ping trust/special-issues. Good job team :thumbsup:

maya-chen: adding link to logs & traces in the ticket, and a prompt set to reproduce long-prefix memory growth. We'll schedule a canary of continuous-batching behind the new guard in staging next week.

samir-patel: handoff complete. I'll stay standby for 30m then sleep. :zzz:
